_note: FICTIONAL example for tests. No real agency, system or person.

A.answer: The model ranks incoming claims by likely missing documents so staff can request them earlier. Baseline: a median of 41 days to first contact in the current manual process (agency workload report, fictional). Target: under 20 days, measured monthly on all claims.

B.answer: Training data are three years of closed claim files with document checklists; 2 percent of records were dropped for missing outcomes. The data include age and disability status, which are protected classes; neither is a model input. The dataset will not be released as an open government data asset because it holds personal records.

C.answer: Risk: claimants whose files resemble rare claim types may be ranked low and wait longer. Mitigation: no claim can be closed or denied by the tool; every claim keeps its place in the manual queue. Privacy impacts are covered by the system's existing PIA. Not using the tool keeps current delays.

D.answer: Reassessment every 12 months and after any retraining, new data source, or change in claim types covered. Each reassessment repeats the subgroup wait-time comparison from pre-deployment testing.

E.answer: Direct costs: one analyst at half time and existing cloud hosting. Expected savings: fewer follow-up letters, estimated from the pilot once measured; no savings are claimed before then.

F.answer: Reviewed by the agency's evaluation office, which did not build the tool. Concern raised: wait times for claimants over 75 were not reported separately. Response: added as a monitored subgroup. The full comments are attached and were shared with the risk owner.

G.answer: Risk accepted for a 12-month deployment, subject to the monitoring in item D.
